To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
peptide vaccines can be harmful to mice that are preimmune to LCMV.
the administration of synthetic peptide to mice immune to LMCV or vaccinia results in a rapid and profound hypotermia that is mediated by CD8 T cells and that can be life-threatening.

the administration of peptides to mice previously infected with LCMVM or vaccinia virus can lead to the rapid and synchronous activation of virus-specific CD8+ T cells, which can cause hypothermia, enterocyte apoptosis, and death.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunological mechanisms of disease and the development of new therapeutic interventions for autoimmune disease and cancer.
understanding the mechanisms of CD8+ T cell mediated immunopathology and developing strategies to prevent it.
the mechanisms of CD8 T cell mediated immunopathology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the administration of peptides to mice immune to LMCV or vaccinia causes serious CD8+ T cell-mediated, Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF)-dependent immunopathology.
peptide vaccination of mice immune for LCMV or Vaccinia virus can cause serious, TNF-mediated, CD8 T cell mediated immunopathology, and this can be fatal.
peptide vaccination of mice immune for LCMV or VV causes serious CD8+ T cell-mediated, and TNF-dependent, immunopathology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the administration of a peptide to virus-immunized mice can cause a rapid and massive activation of preexisting CD8 T cells and that this can lead to a serious, and sometimes lethal, immunopathology.
peptide vaccination of mice with a preexisting pool of virus-specific CD8+ T cells can cause serious immunopathology, and that TNF is the major mediator of this effect.
the activation of a pool of preexisting CD8 T cells by a peptide vaccine can cause serious, and even fatal, immunopathology.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the administration of peptides designed to induce CD8 T cell immunity to virus-immune hosts can be extremely dangerous, and this is particularly true when the virus induces large numbers of CD8 T cells.
peptide vaccination of virus-immune recipients may be dangerous, and we recommend that it be avoided.
immunopathology may be a significant risk for individuals with preexisting CD8 T cell immunity to a pathogen.
